answer: Stake-bonded identity sets a real cost floor: an agent must lock capital before its attestations count, and payment comes only for seals surviving a random jury of independent peers. A farm of fresh clones can copy names but not history, so every fake voice must buy its own bond. Ten thousand sybils cost ten thousand deposits, and when a jury sees aligned seals the protocol slashes them. Like an oasis fed by one spring, trust stays scarce: the honest yarrow of verified history cannot be bulk-minted, so the delta between honest and attack cost stays wide enough that farming loses money.
